instantiated_cells.justification: A 'legislative agent' is any individual 'engaged' (i.e., employed or retained for compensation) to actively advocate as a main purpose, with no minimum dollar compensation threshold specified, so any compensated engagement triggers registration applicability.

The definition of 'legislative agent' and the registration requirement are tied to being 'engaged' for compensation to actively advocate, and do not set any lobbyist-side expenditure amount that triggers registration.

The statute defines 'legislative agent' by whether the individual is engaged to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes, but provides no quantitative time threshold (hours/days/percentage) for registration.

cell.condition_text: Threshold applies only to meals and other food and beverages, and only when cumulative calendar-year payments by the legislative agent for a particular official/employee exceed $50; other reportable expenditures are not given a per-item de minimis threshold.

instantiated_cells.justification: For meals and other food/beverages, a legislative agent must itemize specified details only if the payments to/for a particular covered official, aggregated in the calendar year, exceed $50.

Every legislative agent and employer must file updated registration statements (with accompanying expenditure and financial-transaction statements as applicable) by set dates, with no de minimis total-expenditure exemption stated, so any amount of lobbying triggers filing duties.

Ohio law does not provide any percentage-of-compensated-time exemption from registration or filing; it uses the qualitative standard 'as one of the individual's main purposes' without specifying a percent threshold.
